correctness.rationale: For n>=5 the four neighbor sites are distinct. An isolated run forces its two adjacent opposite runs to be isolated, giving a global checkerboard; without isolated runs a length-two run cannot meet the threshold at its boundary. Every run of length at least three is stable. Marked type-one run starts and binomial compositions prove the exact S_{n,m} sum with divisor k. The six-state matrix is primitive and has characteristic polynomial (t^3-t^2-1)(t^3-t^2+1), giving H_n~lambda^n. A standalone checker completed 134474 exact assertions; this finite test is not substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The asserted contribution is the full binomial population-resolved enumeration and its exact Perron asymptotic, not the earlier-known stability of large homogeneous runs. Direct comparisons with four relevant primary works, including the more general 2022 fixed-point structural theorem, found the stated exact census and entropy absent. Earlier run criteria imply part of the structural proof but do not state the composition count. Historical equivalent-table risk remains.
residual_risks: General structural results could make the new exact count a short corollary, even without the explicit n,m formula having been previously printed.
An unlocated historical automata sequence, OEIS entry, or transfer-matrix enumeration could provide the exact counts.
The theorem counts static complete satisfaction, not swap-dynamics absorbing states or reachable equilibrium probabilities.
The independent audit of mathematical correctness and historical priority has not been performed.

value.rationale: Conservation of the population balance under Schelling swaps makes all S_{n,m} coefficients a natural, model-specific observable. The complete fixed-density census quantifies how many configurations can satisfy every resident at any population ratio and distinguishes minimum-run configurations from checkerboards. Perron entropy gives the exact exponential rarity of fully satisfied uniform layouts. The result is a motivated complete classification of a natural invariant, not a selected small parameter or a mere known-table recomputation.
